text:
Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on massive amounts of text from books, websites, and articles. They learn patterns in language, which lets them predict the next word in a sentence. When you type a prompt—a question or instruction—the model uses these patterns to generate a detailed, human-like response.

Prompt engineering is the skill of writing clear, specific prompts to get better answers. LLMs can summarize, translate, and even write creative text, but they have limits. They don't truly understand meaning; they can make up facts, and their knowledge stops at their training date. So, while powerful, they are tools that need careful use and fact-checking.
